text.p: Swiss watchmaker TAG Heuer SA said overall watch sales for 1996 totalled 717,000 units, up from 703,000 the previous year.
Sales totalled 419.7 million francs in 1996 versus 379.6 million in 1995.

In a statement accompanying 1996 results which were released in the U.S. on Tuesday and in Zurich on Wednesday, TAG Heuer said unit sales rose 17.9 percent in the Americas and 15.5 percent in Europe. In Asia and Australasia, growth increased 3.1 percent. The weak yen undermined duty-free and tourist sales in Asia.
Net income on a non-proforma basis was reported at 26.2 million francs in 1996, down from 75.7 million in 1995.
The company reported proforma net income at 60.5 million Swiss francs in 1996 versus 52.3 million in 1995.
The proforma income is based on roughly 5.38 million shares outstanding, and is equal to 11.24 francs per share, or $0.83 for each American Depositary Share (ADS).
On a comparable basis, proforma net income was 52.3 milion francs in 1995. This was equal to 9.71 francs per share, or $0.72 per ADS.
TAG Heuer also said it had reduced its net debt level to 116.4 million Swiss francs as of December 31, 1996 from 325.3 million francs in 1995.
TAG Heuer went public in September, and is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Swiss bourses.
